title: Inclusive recruitment: attracting candidates
summary: How to advertise a role so that a wide range of people see it, and how to give applicants what they need to apply.

sections.title: Why where you advertise matters
sections.body:
Where a job is advertised decides who sees it. An advert in one place reaches only the people who use that place.
The aim is to reach a wide range of people, so that the best candidates for the job are among those who apply.
key_points: Where you advertise decides who sees the job
The aim is a wide range of candidates

sections.title: Advertise in at least two ways
sections.body:
Advertise in at least two different ways or places. A print newspaper and a jobs website together reach more people than either one alone.
Check that your chosen channels, taken together, reach a mix of people.
key_points: Use at least two different ways or places
Check that the channels together reach a mix of people

sections.title: Do not rely on social media alone
sections.body:
Social media is useful, but relying only on it can miss applicants who do not use it.
Online adverts may only be seen by certain age groups or backgrounds. Combine online posts with other routes.
key_points: Relying only on social media misses some applicants
Online adverts may reach only certain groups
Combine online posts with other routes

sections.title: Neutral job titles and wording
sections.body:
Use neutral job titles, and describe the skills the role needs rather than the type of person you want.
Avoid gendered job titles, and avoid wording based on nationality, because both can put people off applying.
key_points: Describe the skills, not the type of person
Avoid gendered titles and nationality-based wording

sections.title: Share what applicants need
sections.body:
Share the job description, the person specification and the equality and diversity monitoring form with applicants.
When applicants can see the role and the process, they understand what is expected and are more likely to apply with confidence.
key_points: Share the job description and person specification
Share the equality and diversity monitoring form
Clear information helps people apply with confidence

sections.title: Look at who applies
sections.body:
After the advert has been out for a while, look at the people who have applied. If the pool is narrow, widen the places you advertise and review the wording of the advert.
This is a check that should be repeated for every vacancy, not only the first.
key_points: Widen the channels and review the wording if the pool is narrow

questions.prompt: How many different ways or places should a job be advertised in?
options: At least two different ways or places
questions.explanation: Advertise in at least two different ways or places, so that more people see the job.

questions.prompt: Why should a job advert not rely only on social media?
options: Social media cannot be used for jobs
It may miss applicants who do not use it
Social media posts cannot include a job title
questions.explanation: Relying only on social media can miss applicants who do not use it.
Sales assistant is a neutral title. Salesman and barmaid are gendered titles.

questions.prompt: What helps applicants understand the process?
options: Sharing the job description, person specification and monitoring form
Asking applicants to guess the requirements
questions.explanation: Sharing the job description, the person specification and the monitoring form helps applicants understand the role and the process.

questions.prompt: What should a job advert focus on?
options: The type of person the employer wants
A personal description of the owner
questions.explanation: Describing the skills the role needs keeps the advert focused on the job.
